```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

brandkit renders PDFs through Quarto's built-in Typst engine, so no LaTeX is
needed (Quarto 1.8 or later). Quarto's own `_brand.yml` support colours and sets
the fonts of headings, links and body text; brandkit adds a Typst format
extension for what it leaves out: a title area, code styling, coloured
footers, and, for posters, a whole page layout.

## Three formats

```{r}
library(brandkit)

create_brand_quarto_pdf(path = "my-report")         # full-bleed striped banner
create_brand_quarto_print_pdf(path = "my-report")   # plain masthead, for paper
create_brand_quarto_poster(path = "my-poster")      # landscape sheet, A0 by default
```

| | `create_brand_quarto_pdf()` | `create_brand_quarto_print_pdf()` | `create_brand_quarto_poster()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Format | `brandkit-typst` | `brandkit-print-typst` | `brandkit-poster-typst` |
| Extension | `_extensions/brandkit/` | `_extensions/brandkit-print/` | `_extensions/brandkit-poster/` |
| Example file | `report-pdf.qmd` | `report-print.qmd` | `poster.qmd` |
| Title | full-bleed diagonal-stripe banner | plain masthead | plain type on the sheet |
| Corner ornaments | no | first page | yes |
| Best for | screen | printing | one large sheet |

All three share the same template files, so the brand colours, code styling,
coloured headings and type ramp match. The formats can live in one project:
switch a document's `format:` key to render it another way. The `.typ` files are
plain text copied into your project, so you can edit them (margins, title page,
footer).

PDFs have no light/dark toggle, so plots are baked in in whichever mode you give
`brand_quarto_setup()`. Widgets (plotly, DT, leaflet) don't apply; use static
ggplot2 plots and `knitr::kable()` or gt tables.

## The striped PDF

```yaml
---
title: "My Report"
subtitle: "A branded PDF"
author: "Your Name"
date: today
format:
  brandkit-typst:
    toc: false
---
```

```{r}
brand_quarto_setup()   # in the setup chunk
```

```{r}
quarto::quarto_render("report-pdf.qmd")
```

Page one opens with a full-bleed title banner: a diagonal-stripe field, drawn as
Typst polygons rather than an image, primary-coloured behind the title and
switching to secondary-coloured stripes past an angled seam. The logo, if there
is one, sits inline in it. With no title the banner is skipped and the logo
becomes a plain corner mark on page one. The extension also gives you coloured
headings, a footer with the title and page number, and rounded code blocks that
use the brand's border radius.

The generated `_extension.yml` carries the brand's base font size and radius, so
re-run the function after changing the brand. Existing files are kept unless you
pass `overwrite = TRUE`, but a stale font size and radius are brought back up to
date on every re-run.

## The print-friendly PDF

`create_brand_quarto_print_pdf()` is the "drift" look for paper. Instead of the
banner it opens with a plain masthead (the logo on the right, the title in the
brand's primary, the subtitle, a short bar, then the author and date) and frames
the first page with a pair of soft corner ornaments.

It prints well for three reasons: nothing is full-bleed, so no ink goes near an
ordinary printer's unprintable edge; there is no solid panel to show through
lighter paper; and the ornaments are drawn at low opacity, so the header uses a
fraction of the striped banner's ink. The ornaments appear on the first page
only; the running footer starts on page two. The masthead is flow content, so a
long title simply wraps.

One caveat for print: Quarto fills the page with `_brand.yml`'s
`color.background`, independently of the ornaments. If your brand's background
isn't white, that tint is itself full-bleed and will clip at the printer's
edge, so set `color.background` to white for a print-targeted brand.

```yaml
format:
  brandkit-print-typst:
    toc: false
```

## Posters

```{r}
create_brand_quarto_poster(path = "my-poster", paper = "a0", columns = 3)
```

`paper` is one of `"a0"` to `"a4"` (always landscape). It still is a plain
`.qmd`: knitr chunks, `brand_quarto_setup()`, `theme_brand()` and the palettes
work as in a report. What differs follows from it being one big sheet:

- **Corner ornaments instead of a title panel.** A pair of soft shapes, top
  right and bottom left, in the brand's colours; the title is plain type.
- **Page columns.** The body flows down column one, then two, then three; the
  masthead spans them.
- **Every `##` section is a card**: a tinted panel with a primary header bar and
  the brand's corner radius, grouped by the `poster.lua` filter. A card never
  splits across columns. Mark a heading `## Something {.plain}` to opt it out.
- **Type sized to the measure.** About 70 characters to a line, so the body size
  follows from `paper` and `columns` (A0 with three columns gives roughly 36 pt;
  with four, 26 pt), with a viewing-distance floor under it (24 pt on A0) and the
  masthead 1.6 times larger.
- **No running footer.** `poster-footer:` in the YAML adds an optional standing
  band for affiliations, funding or a URL.

```yaml
---
title: "A Branded Conference Poster"
subtitle: "Landscape, three columns, all inferred from _brand.yml"
author: "Your Name"
date: today
poster-footer: "Department of Everything | you@example.org"
format:
  brandkit-poster-typst:
    columns: 3
execute:
  echo: false        # a poster shows findings, not source
---
```

`paper` and `columns` are arguments to the scaffold, not YAML, because the type
scale is baked into the extension. Setting `papersize:` in a document changes the
sheet but not the type sized for it, so re-run the function instead.

A poster is a fixed sheet and Typst won't shrink content to fit: material that
overruns spills onto a second page, as does any single card taller than a
column. Cut content, or move to four columns.

## Corner ornaments

The ornaments are SVG drawn from `_brand.yml`. For the Typst formats they are
generated at scaffold time next to the extension (`drift-top-right.svg` and
`drift-bottom-left.svg`) and drawn as the page background; re-run the scaffold
after changing the brand and they are rewritten if they changed. The top-right
piece leads with the primary colour and the bottom-left with the secondary, so
a sheet is balanced rather than mirrored. Each shape is a full brand colour at a
low opacity, so the extra shades come from overlaps, and one `softness` value
controls the whole drawing.

The generator is exported for anywhere an SVG will do:

```{r}
cat(brand_ornament("drift", "top-right"))
brand_ornament("drift", "bottom-left", softness = 0.1, file = "corner.svg")
brand_ornaments_tag()    # the pair, as HTML for a web page
```

Posters use a lower softness (0.12) than the function's default (0.17), since
the same opacity over an A0 sheet reads as large flat blocks.

### Text on an ornament

A short line (a brand name, say, up to 16 characters) can be set along the swell
of one ornament, in capitals in the heading font, on the part of the largest
circle the swell doesn't cover. Set it in the configurator's *Meta & Logo* tab,
or in `_brand.yml`:

```yaml
meta:
  ornament-label: Acme Group
  ornament-label-corner: bottom-left   # omit for the default, top-right
```

`ornament-label-corner` also accepts `top` and `bottom`. The text reads left to
right on either corner. `brand_ornament()` draws the brand's text on the corner
the brand picks; a `label =` you pass is drawn on whichever corner you ask for,
and `label = NULL` draws none.
